## Outcome

Give the existing React app and background workers a typed, authenticated boundary for the hosted platform.

Scope: V1 planned work; implementation is not complete. [Agreed specification](https://linear.app/r1cco/document/v1-platform-specification-agreed-scope-22e7266690a9).

## Existing code/components to reuse

- `app/CONVENTIONS.md`
- `app/src/module/profile/types.ts`
- `app/src/module/scout/types.ts`
- `app/src/module/scout/result.ts`

## Required behavior and boundaries

- Keep app/ and existing UI modules in place. Add a TypeScript Fastify modular monolith and shared runtime-validated command/query schemas; agree names and package paths within the documented repository proposal.
- Define session-derived workspace context, structured errors, expected revisions, idempotency keys, correlation IDs, and bounded worker observations. Client or model payloads never select an authorized workspace.
- Separate commands from read models and external effects; use backend adapters for credentials. Define ports that later auth/database issues wire to real infrastructure.
- Include a minimal workspace-scoped posting identity/snapshot/import contract shared by profile/dossier import and later scout runs; define unknown legacy dates and assessment provenance without implementing source adapters.

## Dependencies / blocked-by issues

None. Establishes a shared foundation for later work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Malformed payloads and untrusted workspace identifiers fail validation; a command cannot accept model-generated authorization.
- [ ] Document contracts for expired sessions, conflicts, duplicate commands, cancellation, and waiting for user AI without leaking private values.
- [ ] Keep API response types independent of filesystem handles; no required frontend relocation.

## Validation procedure

1. Add focused contract/schema checks and an API boundary example in the implementation PR; exercise invalid requests and map structured errors to current Result conventions.
2. Review module ownership with the login/auth and database implementers before wiring infrastructure.

## Owning documentation references

Local repository paths; these changes are not yet published to GitHub. This issue includes the required scope so work can start from Linear.

issues.title: Containerize PostgreSQL and establish Drizzle migrations
issues.outcome: Provide durable self-hosted persistence and migration discipline for platform state.
behavior: Run PostgreSQL in Docker Compose with a private network and persistent volume on the owner's VPS; use Drizzle schemas and migrations.

Establish workspace keys, permanent command receipts, append-only event/revision storage, projections, and durable work intent. Commit domain decisions, receipts and work intent atomically; pg-boss delivery remains separate from permanent domain idempotency.
Keep sensitive documents outside events and nginx assets. Use least-privilege runtime access and explicit migration ownership; document backup compatibility.
Provide the shared workspace-scoped posting/alias/snapshot and import-receipt persistence primitives consumed first by dossier import. Later scout-run orchestration builds on those primitives.
acceptance: Fresh install and migration of an existing database produce the same schema without dropping user data.
Injected failure rolls back decision/receipt/work intent together; concurrent duplicate command keys produce one logical effect.
Queue retention or job deletion cannot permit a previously completed domain command to apply again; cross-workspace key collisions remain isolated.
validation: Run integration checks against a disposable PostgreSQL container for migrations, transaction rollback, concurrency and duplicate replay.
Rehearse recovery from an interrupted migration on a backup copy; document the safe deployment sequence.

issues.title: Implement Google sign-in and emailed login codes
issues.outcome: Let pilot users sign in without a Job Kit password.
behavior: Integrate self-hosted Better Auth with Google and emailed one-time codes through the owner's existing SMTP account; secrets are deployment configuration.
Use secure session cookies, CSRF/state controls, bounded code lifetimes and abuse protection. Better Auth owns verified identity linking; never merge candidates by an application-level email string.
Expose recoverable login cancellation, invalid/expired codes, SMTP failure, logout and session expiry. Google and email are authentication methods for the user, not separate candidate identities.
acceptance: Both login methods establish and renew sessions; logout invalidates access. No password signup/reset UI or password credential storage is introduced.
Expired/reused codes, cancelled Google consent, callback mismatch, and failed SMTP delivery are safe and understandable.
Unverified identity cannot claim an existing account; supported method-linking preserves the same authenticated user.
validation: Exercise Google and SMTP end-to-end in a controlled deployment with test accounts; verify cookie and callback behavior.
Test expired/reused codes, rate limiting, session revocation, verified identity linkage, and unavailable SMTP without logging codes/tokens.

specification.content:
# Job Kit AI V1 — agreed platform specification

Decision snapshot: 2026-09-21. **Implementation: not implemented.** These requirements describe the platform to build, not verified integrations. Local documentation is not yet published to GitHub; this document and the linked issues carry the agreed scope in Linear.

## Product outcome and existing baseline

An invited user signs in, connects their own AI, confirms a profile, runs a search, reviews ranked results in the existing dossiers page, and opens the original job posting. The five milestones are Login, Onboarding, AI profile, First scout, and Check matches.

Retain the existing React/Vite application under `app/`, its routes, settings, design system, dossier table/cards/filters/detail and ordinary exports. Migrate filesystem data access to authenticated APIs. The current local skills and folder distribution remain unchanged by this platform plan. Do not require a frontend relocation or redesign.

V1 has no Job Kit companion, desktop application, device pairing, local executor or browser extension. Application preparation/submission and copy-apply-prompt handoff are deferred for a separate post-V1 mechanism review. Gmail and recurring automation are also outside V1. Opening a posting, copying a dossier or exporting data is never evidence of application submission.

## Accepted architecture

Run platform services on the owner's VPS with Docker Compose: Fastify TypeScript API, PostgreSQL, Drizzle, Better Auth, and pg-boss. Keep the existing `.github/workflows/deploy-app.yml` as the deployment baseline. No Supabase, Trigger.dev Cloud, managed database/auth/workflow/browser/storage requirement remains in the selected design. External Google sign-in, AI providers, SMTP and public job sites remain explicit integrations.

Better Auth supplies Google sign-in and emailed one-time codes through the owner's existing SMTP account; there are no passwords. An approved-email pilot gate applies on the server. Provision one private workspace per authenticated user idempotently, including concurrent first login. The auth library's verified linking owns identity association; Job Kit must not merge accounts by matching email strings.

Resolve workspace authority from authenticated server context on every private query, command, file access and worker claim. Clients and models cannot choose an authorized workspace. Keep provider credentials encrypted behind backend adapters, with keys outside the database and secrets excluded from prompts, events, logs, browser storage and queue payloads.

Private persistent volumes hold documents and evidence outside nginx's public asset directory. Serve them through authorized APIs. Define retention/deletion and rehearse coordinated database/file/key recovery; do not invent availability or capacity guarantees.

Selective event sourcing is accepted. Important confirmed revisions and decisions are immutable; transient data and private documents remain separately controlled/deletable. Commit domain decisions, command receipts and durable work intent transactionally. pg-boss transports durable work; queue retention is not permanent idempotency. Dispatch retries, worker leases/fencing and accepted-result uniqueness must tolerate duplicate delivery. Replay reconstructs recorded decisions without model calls, searches, mail, document generation or external dispatch.

Python Browser Use runs dedicated Chrome processes/profiles on the VPS, isolated from Hermes and from other users/attempts. Use bounded scoped work and validated observations, private CDP, network restrictions, renewable claims, cleanup and persistent checkpoints. Start the coexistence experiment with one slot; actual capacity is unverified.

## Milestone 01 · Login

An approved user signs in using Google or an emailed code and reaches the right setup or application route. Preserve the login reference's split layout and visual hierarchy while simplifying email actions to Send code and Verify code. No password actions are added.

Recover expired/reused codes, cancelled Google login, unavailable SMTP and expired sessions. Deny unapproved/unverified identities without revealing another user's data. Shared API/contracts, database/migrations and deployment/backup work attach here as their first consuming milestone. Shared posting/import contracts are established early so dossier imports do not depend on later scout orchestration.

## Milestone 02 · Onboarding and AI connections

Users must connect their own AI before profile creation. Persist setup progress and distinguish authorization from real execution readiness. Target the full provider/method set from commit-tools commit `07321aa31a734bbe6e52fa0776666d1df81eaee9`:

| Provider | Requested methods |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAI | Device login or API key |
| Gemini | OAuth or API key |
| Anthropic | Pasted Claude setup token or API key |
| xAI | Device login or API key |

Optional Claude token generation in an external terminal followed by paste is accepted; it does not require installing Job Kit. The local CLI source is a reference, not evidence that a hosted route is supported or authorized.

Each provider ticket must prove both requested hosted authentication methods and bounded execution, record versions, eligibility/restrictions and redacted evidence, and exercise expiry/revocation, quota, cancellation and failure. A failed experiment remains a visible blocker; the provider target must not silently shrink. Choose a compatible model for each required route rather than promising every model offered by a provider.

The selected user AI powers profile and browser work. If unavailable, preserve work and wait for reconnect or a manual account/route switch. Never automatically change accounts or billing. TypeSafe is a separate platform-funded matching service; its documented fallback is the selected user AI. General Job Kit-funded AI is a separate Post-V1 issue.

## Milestone 03 · AI profile

Accept a text-based PDF CV or manual intake. Scanned/unreadable PDFs use manual entry; OCR and other upload formats are outside V1. Upload/extract privately with bounded limits and cleanup. Extracted/model-proposed facts remain proposals until the user explicitly confirms them.

Cover existing questionnaire fields: identity/contact, experience, projects, skills, languages, education, compensation, availability, country-specific work eligibility, roles, locations, work models, source preferences/exclusions and CV tailoring preferences. Optional story names and observations remain supported. Do not infer legal eligibility, language proficiency, demographic/EEO data or unsupported impact claims from silence.

Publish immutable confirmed whole-profile snapshots with explicit revision conflicts. Required search basics are target roles, locations and work-model preferences; optional unknowns remain unknown. Save progress across interruption and provider failure.

Import existing profile and dossier formats with previews, conflict review, deduplication and source provenance. An incomplete legacy corpus is not a complete event history; never invent prior confirmations, dates, submissions or accepted current assessments. Retain editable profile exports and ordinary dossier exports independently of future application mechanisms. Migrate existing profile/settings/answers/resumes/recommendations data access through APIs.

## Milestone 04 · First scout

Offer a verified suggested employer catalog and supported user-supplied company links. Support Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby public HTTP adapters with explicit URL rules, pagination/completeness, identifiers/aliases, canonical posting links, description evidence and truthful dates. Unsupported links remain visibly unsupported.

Select and prove the first public browser source end-to-end using isolated VPS Browser Use and the user's selected AI. Record model/auth compatibility, source evidence, limits and host resource measurements. Login walls/challenges return blocked coverage; V1 does not take over authenticated browser sessions or bypass them.

A run pins confirmed profile and search configuration revisions. Persist posting identity, observations, source progress and snapshots before durable independent matching handoff. Distinguish empty/partial/blocked/failed/cancelled/complete discovery from assessment progress. Scoring failures or thresholds cannot erase discovery evidence; incomplete scans do not close postings.

Retry and cancellation preserve committed results, permanently deduplicate commands/delivery and fence late worker observations. Refreshing the UI restores persisted progress. Source retries need not repeat matching and matching retries need not search again.

## Milestone 05 · Check matches

Use TypeSafe classification with the existing deterministic Python scorer behind versioned JSON contracts. Pin profile, posting, policy/rubric, classifier and scorer versions. Preserve hard filters, factor weights, decision bands and confidence-floor behavior. Unknown/unscorable facts are not zero. Validate both schema and evidence semantics, including the existing review gates for fit at least 75, confidence below 0.7 or uncertain factors; rescore corrections.

When TypeSafe is unavailable, use the selected user AI and show engine/provenance. If that connection also fails, preserve the request in a waiting/recoverable state. Keep previous accepted assessments as history. New confirmed profile revisions automatically trigger deduplicated reassessment; draft edits and page reads do not execute models.

Reuse the existing dossiers table/cards/filters/detail/export/Open posting. Apply filters and ordering globally before pagination:
1. Current accepted 0–100 fit descending.
2. Publication date descending; when unknown, first-discovered time with an honest date label.
3. Stable posting ID tie-breaker.

Rows without a current accepted score follow current ranked matches as one group ordered by the same recency and ID rules. Pending, failed, waiting, unscored and outdated states remain distinguishable. A stale high score is historical and cannot outrank a current accepted match. Scout coverage 0–10 and confidence stay separately labeled.

## Completion evidence and release blockers

The backlog contains 35 V1 issues (6 Login, 7 Onboarding, 6 AI profile, 9 First scout, 7 Check matches), plus separate Post-V1 funded-AI and application-mechanism issues. All start in Backlog, unassigned, with no invented deadline or estimate. Existing Scout reliability and R1C-227–R1C-230 remain unchanged.

Every issue states outcome, existing components, boundaries, blocking dependencies, failure acceptance, validation and owning local docs. The final pilot verification depends on the implemented journey and all required provider/source proofs.

Required evidence covers:
- Two-user workspace/private-file isolation and approved-email login through both methods.
- Unknown facts, explicit confirmation, conflicting/repeated imports and editable exports.
- Worker interruption, queue outages/cleanup, duplicate commands/delivery, lease expiry and cancellation.
- Provider failure, saved work, reconnect/manual switching and TypeSafe fallback provenance.
- Global ranking/pagination, outdated assessments and automatic reassessment.
- Replay with external effects disabled; backup/restore and Hermes/browser isolation.

No integration or deployment is claimed to work until those future implementation checks pass.

## Owning documentation

Local paths identify design ownership; they are not assertions that the files are already published to GitHub:
- `docs/decisions/0002-selective-event-sourcing.md`, `0007-web-only-platform.md`, `0008-self-hosted-platform.md`.
- `docs/architecture/overview.md`, `persistence.md`, `execution.md`, `identity-and-data.md`, `browser-workers.md`, `repository.md`.
- `docs/domain/workspace.md`, `candidate.md`, `discovery.md`, `evaluation.md`.
- `docs/delivery/roadmap.md` and the five numbered step briefs; `docs/delivery/linear-backlog.json` preserves creation identifiers for safe resumption.

Provider reference: [commit-tools authentication source](https://github.com/rafaeelricco/commit-tools/tree/07321aa31a734bbe6e52fa0776666d1df81eaee9/src/infra/auth). Dated research and superseded ADRs remain historical evidence and cannot override this V1 scope.

## Planned web platform V1

[Read the agreed V1 specification](https://linear.app/r1cco/document/v1-platform-specification-agreed-scope-22e7266690a9). - **02 · Onboarding:** encrypted own-AI connections and all four provider proofs, guided setup, waiting/reconnect/manual switching.
- **03 · AI profile:** PDF/manual intake, explicit confirmation, immutable revisions, reviewed profile/dossier imports, existing settings migration and editable export.
